articles.headline: Man City down Sunderland in eight-goal thriller
articles.description: Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100 per cent Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.
articles.body:
Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100 per cent Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.

In a game characterised by poor defending, City struggled to kill off the fired-up visitors at the Etihad Stadium, with Brobbey a constant thorn in their side.

Ultimately two goals from Antoine Semenyo and a late strike from Erling Haaland finished the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki were also on target.

Unlike in last week's Manchester derby, City failed to assert control against a Sunderland side clearly not drained by their midweek Europa League excursions.

For new manager Enzo Maresca, however, it was at least a fifth successiv

articles.headline: European soccer live updates: Man City, Liverpool in action
articles.description: The weekend continues with Man City going clear at the top of the Premier League and Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola winning on his return to Bournemouth.
articles.body:
The weekend of soccer across Europe continues!

In the Premier League, Manchester City will spend the international break three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table after a thrilling 5-3 win over Sunderland, while Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola got a 1-0 win on his return to former club Bournemouth. Next up, Manchester United visit Fulham as they look to bounce back after losing the derby and getting eliminated midweek in the Carabao Cup.

In LaLiga, Atlético Madrid host Real Madrid in the first Madrid derby of the season, while Juventus meet Atalanta in Serie A. In the Bundesliga, Bayer Leverkusen face RB Leipzig before the day concludes in Ligue 1 with Marseille hosting Paris Saint-Germain in Le Classique.

Enjoy all the updates from Sunday's matches.

articles.headline: Leeds and Crystal Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
articles.body:
Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the season but had to settle for a point from a goalless draw with much-improved Crystal Palace at Elland Road.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spurned Leeds' best chance when firing straight at Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez in the second half after visiting defender Tyrick Mitchell was denied a winner by VAR.

These are heady times at Leeds after they climbed up to third in the table last week after dismantling Newcastle 4-1 and although they are only five games into their second season back in the top flight, expectation was high among fans before kick-off.

But Palace turned in one of their best displays of the season and will consider themselves unlucky to have secured only one point after creating the better chances.

Given Palace had conceded more goals - 11 - than any other side in the top flight this season, it was no surprise they sat deep when out of possession in the early exchanges.

But they were dangerous on the counter-attack and it took a superb recovery tackle from Tarik Muharemovic to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen, while Leeds squandered early pressure with poor set-piece deliveries.

James Trafford was the first goalkeeper forced into a save when diving low to hold Daichi Kamada's shot and with Leeds struggling to find an end product, Pierre Sage will have been the happier of the two managers at half-time.

Trafford was at full stretch low down to brilliantly turn away Yeremy Pino's free-kick soon after the restart and Kamada's shot flew narrowly wide.

Palace were then denied a deserved lead when Tyrick Mitchell lashed home after Anan Khalaili's cross had deflected off Muharemovic.

Referee Adam Herczeg, taking charge of his first Premier League game, awarded a goal, but it was ruled out by VAR, who deemed Khalaili to have been offside.

Leeds almost snatched the lead after their let-off as Calvert-Lewin fired his point-blank effort from James Justin's cross straight at Palace keeper Benitez.

Palace continued to pose Leeds problems, with midfield lynchpin Adam Wharton central to their promptings while Kamada's header span the wrong side of a post as the home fans grew increasingly frustrated.

Another timely tackle from Muharemovic thwarted Palace substitute Ismaïla Sarr in the penalty area as Leeds failed to carve out another chance against an organised, water-tight defence.

articles.headline: Alexander Isak winner for Liverpool on Andoni Iraola return to Bournemouth
articles.description: Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.

The Sweden international broke the deadlock with his fourth goal of the season in the 57th minute after some fine work by Cody Gakpo in the build-up to extend the Reds' unbeaten run and reward Iraola with a second win.

Isak has now already scored more Premier League goals in their first five league matches than he did across his entire previous top-flight campaign.

Iraola left for Anfield after three seasons with the Cherries, capped off by leading the club to a maiden European berth last season.

He was greeted warmly as he emerged before kick-off, exchanging a hug with his German successor Marco Rose.

articles.headline: Bruno Guimarães: Arsenal performance in Brighton defeat not fit for champions
articles.description: Bruno Guimarães said Arsenal's "unacceptable" performance in their defeat at Brighton was not fit for a Premier League champions' shirt.
articles.headlineJa: ブルーノ・ギマランイス：ブライトン戦に敗れたアーセナルのパフォーマンスは王者にふさわしくない
articles.descriptionJa: ブルーノ・ギマランイスは、ブライトン戦でのアーセナルの「受け入れがたい」敗戦パフォーマンスは、プレミアリーグ王者のユニフォームにふさわしくないと語りました。
articles.body:
Bruno Guimarães said Arsenal's "unacceptable" performance in their defeat at Brighton was not fit for a Premier League champions' shirt.

Arsenal's 100% start to the new season ended in abrupt fashion as Brighton put Mikel Arteta's side to the sword with a brilliant 3-0 victory.

The Gunners, who arrived at the Amex Stadium with seven wins from their seven matches so far, were well off the pace.

And Guimaraes, after making his first league start for the Gunners since his £75 million ($100m) transfer from Newcastle, said: "We are very disappointed, and we have to learn from our mistakes because we were far away off our level.

"We were too sloppy with the ball, didn't win any duels. And we cannot accept this while wearing this shirt of a champion. We cannot repeat this.

"It's a lesson for us because I think we've been on a good run so far. We'd won every game, but this is a game to forget and we have to improve. It was a bad day at the office for everyone, and we have to say sorry to the fans because it wasn't good enough."

Brighton supporters revelled in their fine win against Arsenal and goaded Arteta's men with chants of "Are you Tottenham in disguise?" and "Champions of England, you're having a laugh."

Manager Arteta will now have three weeks to stew on Arsenal's heaviest defeat since 2023, with his side not back in action until a home match against Leeds on October 10.

However, defender Ezri Konsa has challenged his teammates to use the extended international break to "reflect and learn" on a result which derails any suggestion Arsenal will canter to a second league title in as many seasons.

"We have high standards here and we let them go," Konsa said. "We are very disappointed to lose and to concede three goals is not like us. As a defender, I pride myself on keeping clean sheets.

- Arsenal's aura of champions evaporates after Brighton thrash them 3-0 

- Brighton vs. Arsenal player ratings as Gunners slump to defeat against Seagulls 

- Arsenal 'in trouble from first throw-in' at Brighton - Mikel Arteta

"We conceded two goals from outside of the box. They were two very good strikes.

"But there were moments in those two goals where we could have pressed the ball more, and put more pressure on the ball.

"It's the Premier League, when you give quality players outside the box time and they shoot, it can go in.

"But it is important we use this time now to reflect as individuals, we have to move on very quickly and know that when we do come back there is a lot to learn and a lot to fix from this game."

Each week during the 2026 NFL season, these fantasy football IDP rankings will be updated by fantasy analysts Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.

We've split up our fantasy football rankings by traditional IDP (individual defensive players) positions: defensive line, linebacker and defensive back. Scoring systems can vary greatly in IDP formats, so these rankings are based on the following scoring criteria:

Solo tackle: 1.5 points

Assisted tackle: 0.75 points

Tackle for loss: 2 points

Sack: 4 points

Interception: 5 points

Forced fumble: 4 points

Fumble recovery: 4 points

Defensive TD: 6 points
